items.title: Len Manno Interview, 1959-02-06
items.q: we have Glenn Hughes we call him gosh Hughes who plays real fine Dixie trombone

ctx.x: uh well uh just like I say uh our piano players boiled on down uh I told you by George Bouchon uh uh and um gee you caught me off guard here I have to stop and think for a minute um well Jack Sharp was real popular down there Jack was a sort of a character and he was uh one of the first people that I knew that became chord conscious in other words he he was he was exploring the possibilities of using different harmonies other than the straight major minor augmented and uh occasionally a diminished and a seventh…

in the run and of course we have Glenn Hughes we call him gosh Hughes who plays real fine Dixie trombone I don't like to use this word tailgate trombone because misleading but he plays real fine Dixie trombone another real fine Dixie
trombone player Bill Cummins well what's the difference between Dixie and tailgate I mean you seem to make a distinction in your mind well there's so many of these
